config.problem_statement: Between Jan and Jun 2026, requisitions in the requisition-to-offer process took a median of [baseline] calendar days from approval to first offer, with 1 in 10 exceeding [P90] days, delaying start dates for hiring managers and risking loss of preferred candidates.
config.goal_statement: Reduce median and P90 time to offer to a level agreed with hiring managers by [date] - target pending approval.
config.scope: Approved external requisitions, all business units, opened Jan-Jun 2026
config.exclusions: Cancelled requisitions (counted separately); internal transfers; executive search

findings.label: Calculated result
findings.finding: Median time to offer is 27.0 days (95% CI 25.9-28.1); 1 in 10 cases takes more than 41.5 days.
findings.evidence: 417 completed cases, 05 Jan 2026 - 05 Jul 2026. Kaplan-Meier median including 35 open cases: 27.9 days.
findings.implication: The long tail, not the typical case, drives customer dissatisfaction and backlog. Mean-based reporting would overstate the typical case.
findings.action: Agree the CTQ requirement with customers before setting a target; report median and P90 together.
findings.limitation: Timestamps not yet verified against source; target not approved.

findings.label: Calculated result
findings.finding: 'Open to shortlist' is the longest stage in 45.8% of fully-timestamped cases.
findings.evidence: Pareto of longest stage across 391 cases with all stage timestamps.
findings.implication: Improvement effort is likely to pay back most in this stage - subject to cause validation.
findings.action: Run root-cause workshop and Gemba focused on this stage; collect delay reasons.
findings.limitation: Excludes 64 cases with missing stage timestamps; missingness is not random by unit.

findings.label: Calculated result
findings.finding: No statistically detectable difference in time to offer by business unit (largest median gap 2.4 days, p = 0.130).
findings.evidence: Kruskal-Wallis across 4 groups, epsilon-squared 0.006; proposed practical threshold 5 days.
findings.implication: This does not prove the segments are equal; it means this data cannot distinguish them.
findings.action: Stratify cause analysis by business unit; do not attribute differences to teams or individuals.
findings.limitation: Observational association only; case mix not adjusted; pairwise comparisons need multiplicity adjustment.

findings.label: Calculated result
findings.finding: Time to offer differs by job family: median 31.1 (Engineering) vs 22.9 (Operations) days, a gap of 8.2 days (p < 0.001).
findings.evidence: Kruskal-Wallis across 4 groups, epsilon-squared 0.149; proposed practical threshold 5 days.
findings.implication: Gap exceeds the proposed practical threshold - segment-specific standard work may be needed.
findings.action: Stratify cause analysis by job family; do not attribute differences to teams or individuals.
findings.limitation: Observational association only; case mix not adjusted; pairwise comparisons need multiplicity adjustment.

findings.label: Calculated result
findings.finding: 1 special-cause signal(s) in weekly cohort medians: R1 at week of 19 Jan
findings.evidence: I-MR chart, 24 mature weekly cohorts; centre 27.32, limits 20.08 to 34.57 days.
findings.implication: Investigate what was different in the flagged weeks before treating the baseline as stable.
findings.action: Process owner to review flagged weeks against calendar, volume and system events.
findings.limitation: Weekly medians of completed cases; small weekly n widens natural variation.

findings.label: Verified fact
findings.finding: 5 duplicate rows and 8 chronology errors found in the extract.
findings.evidence: Automated data-quality profile of the immutable raw upload.
findings.implication: Unless corrected, these defects would distort the baseline. They also point to weaknesses in data entry controls.
findings.action: Data owner to correct the source records and confirm the business rules for entering dates.
findings.limitation: Profile detects structural errors only; accuracy needs sample verification.
